newsitem.title: THAILAND: KR Precision sees record earnings in 1997.
newsitem.headline: KR Precision sees record earnings in 1997.

text.p: Thai hard disk suspension manufacturer KR Precision Plc expects to post record earnings in 1997, KRP President Dale Schudel said on Tuesday.
An expected rise in world demand for hard disks and improved utilisation of production facilities would likely raise KRP's output in the first quarter this year, he said.

"We are expecting a record year in terms of earnings and revenues. Things are really starting to happen again this year ...we are looking at producing more than 24 million units this quarter," Schudel told Reuters.
With KRP's new factory due to start commercial production in May, output was expected to rise two million units per month through to at least mid-1998, Schudel said.
KRP achieved previous record output levels in the second quarter of 1995 when quarterly output reached 22 million units, Schudel said.
Difficult market conditions in the hard disk sector in the second half of 1996 and product adjustment to meet client requirements had prevented a return to production level in 1996, he said.

"Last year we had a difficult third quarter but assuming the market allows us to expand smoothly and evenly we hope to be able to increase production by around two million units per month per quarter over the next six or seven quarters," he said.
KRP has recently secured a $25 million loan arranged through Sakura Bank Ltd 's Thai offshore banking unit at 125 basis points above SIBOR, he said.
The loan will finance approximately half of KRP's new 1.5 billion baht, 150,000-square-foot plant. The three-year loan included a one-year interest payment grace period, he said.
Rising output and revenue should help the company meet its short-term financing needs, he said.

The company, supplying Seagate and Read-Rite with hard disk suspensions, is currently seeking to supply a Chinese sub-assembler of components of a new range of cutting edge Western Digital desktop drives, Schudel said.
"Our long term aim is to have 15 percent of the world market by the end of 1998. We currently have around 10 percent," he said.
